All physics of the paper is in the Python package `fluxpy`. The scripts in `scripts/` and `figures_manuscript/` import it and write the numbers, tables and figures; the chapters of the Method section call the same functions. Each module names the section of the paper it implements, and each function that implements an equation quotes it in its docstring.

These pages are generated from the docstrings, signatures and `#:` comments of the code by `docs/build_api.py` (`pixi run api`); `pixi run test` fails if they are out of date. Each entry links to its source on GitHub and shows the source in a collapsible box.

## Top-level names

`import fluxpy` loads the physics modules and makes these names available at the top level:

| Name | Defined in | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`BulkConfig`](#fluxpy.bulk.BulkConfig) | [`fluxpy.bulk`](fluxpy.bulk.md) | The free parameters of one bulk flux run (manuscript Table B1 and Sect. 4.2). |
| [`SegmentConfig`](#fluxpy.aggregate.SegmentConfig) | [`fluxpy.aggregate`](fluxpy.aggregate.md) | How the legs are cut and classified (defaults = the paper). |
| [`air_density`](#fluxpy.util.air_density) | [`fluxpy.util`](fluxpy.util.md) | Dry-air density from the ideal-gas law, $\rho = p / (R_d T)$ [kg m-3]. |
| [`amplitude_matched_config`](#fluxpy.bulk.amplitude_matched_config) | [`fluxpy.bulk`](fluxpy.bulk.md) | Amplitude-matched configuration: alpha_T = 1e-4, the value at which the in-situ bulk estimate reproduces the observed flux amplitude (regression slope 1; manuscript Sect. 4.2). |
| [`amplitude_metrics`](#fluxpy.sensitivity.amplitude_metrics) | [`fluxpy.sensitivity`](fluxpy.sensitivity.md) | Amplitude of an estimate `y` relative to the EC reference `x`: ordinary-least-squares `slope` of y on x (the paper's amplitude metric), `intercept`, and `std_ratio` = sigma_y / sigma_x. |
| [`bulk_richardson_2pt`](#fluxpy.stability.bulk_richardson_2pt) | [`fluxpy.stability`](fluxpy.stability.md) | Two-point bulk Richardson number (manuscript Eq. B3) |
| [`potential_temperature`](#fluxpy.util.potential_temperature) | [`fluxpy.util`](fluxpy.util.md) | Dry potential temperature (Poisson equation; manuscript App. B1, Eq. B1) |
| [`process_legs`](#fluxpy.aggregate.process_legs) | [`fluxpy.aggregate`](fluxpy.aggregate.md) | Cut every leg into segments and compute one row per segment. |
| [`reference_config`](#fluxpy.bulk.reference_config) | [`fluxpy.bulk`](fluxpy.bulk.md) | Reference configuration of the paper: GLGS20, alpha_T = 1e-1 (the conventional value of large-eddy simulations over sea ice), Table B1 roughness set. |
| [`segment_flux`](#fluxpy.eddy_covariance.segment_flux) | [`fluxpy.eddy_covariance`](fluxpy.eddy_covariance.md) | EC sensible heat flux and its random error for one segment. |
| [`segment_spectra`](#fluxpy.qc.segment_spectra) | [`fluxpy.qc`](fluxpy.qc.md) | Spectra of one segment as shown in Fig. A1, plus the integrity-check slope. |
| [`skill_metrics`](#fluxpy.sensitivity.skill_metrics) | [`fluxpy.sensitivity`](fluxpy.sensitivity.md) | Slope, intercept, std_ratio, Pearson r, bias, RMSE, centred RMSE and n of an estimate against the reference, over the pairs where both are finite. |
| [`slope_bootstrap_ci`](#fluxpy.sensitivity.slope_bootstrap_ci) | [`fluxpy.sensitivity`](fluxpy.sensitivity.md) | Percentile-bootstrap 95 % confidence interval of the regression slope. |
| [`to_xarray`](#fluxpy.aggregate.to_xarray) | [`fluxpy.aggregate`](fluxpy.aggregate.md) | DataFrame of `process_legs` -> Dataset indexed by `start_time`, with units. |
| [`turbulence_resolved`](#fluxpy.qc.turbulence_resolved) | [`fluxpy.qc`](fluxpy.qc.md) | Integrity check: True when the w power spectrum follows the inertial-subrange slope, `\|s_w + 5/3\| <= tolerance` (0.4 in the paper). |

## Usage

```python
from fluxpy.eddy_covariance import segment_flux          # one 5 km segment -> H, sigma_rand
from fluxpy.bulk import reference_config, compute_bulk_shf_obs
from fluxpy.sensitivity import skill_metrics              # slope, r, bias, RMSE against the EC flux
```

## Conventions

* Every flux is positive **upward**, from the surface to the atmosphere, in W m⁻². The model-diagnosed ERA5 and CARRA fluxes are sign-flipped once, in [`scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py`](#scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py).
* Physical constants are defined once, in [`fluxpy.util`](fluxpy.util.md), with the values the paper states.
* Temperatures may be passed in °C or K and pressures in hPa or Pa where a docstring says so; the helpers in `fluxpy.util` convert. Everything is computed in float64.
* Variable names of the data files follow [`fluxpy.naming`](fluxpy.naming.md); the symbols are explained in the [glossary](../glossary.md).
